newsitem.title: SWEDEN: No Swedish decision on EMU from finance minister.
newsitem.headline: No Swedish decision on EMU from finance minister.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink gave no indication of Sweden's view towards membership of the European Monetary Union (EMU) in a speech on Thursday, his spokeswoman told Reuters.

Asbrink had said earlier he could not exclude announcing the long-awaited decision at a traditional May Day speech. His spokeswoman quoted him as saying it could be a few more weeks before a decision is announced.

Asbrink's spokeswoman said he faced questions on EMU at a news conference at Ostersund, 560 kms (400 miles) north of Stockholm. "But he did not say anything about Sweden's view. He said a decision could still be a few weeks away," she said.
The Swedish social democratic government is walking a tightrope on EMU. The cabinet is thought to favour it but the party grassroots and Swedish public opinion is largely against membership.
Prime Minister Goran Persson has said the party leadership will make a recommendation this spring about a single currency.
Analysts expect Sweden to take the so-called "soft option" of rejecting joining the first wave of EMU participants but saying Sweden will join at some stage in the future.
